Manual Verification RESULTS — SL/Target Features & Order Types (all 18 cases)

Every backtest exit re-derived across Time · Logic · Price from the order book + the NIFTY 1-second catalog bars — never from what the engine claims — plus a six-caveat execution-realism tier (entry correctness, realistic fills, slippage, gap behaviour, intrabar ordering, P&L realism). MIS / NIFTY, 15:29 IST square-off. Click any case to expand.

✔ ALL 18 CASES PASS — 18 verified across Time · Logic · Price (incl. 2 save-rejection negative tests)
Each case below is a collapsible section — click to expand its per-trade verification, click again to contract. The verdict pill and pass/fail counts sit on every header. The Time·Logic·Price verdict proves the level/trigger/fill; a second execution-realism tier (below, and inside each case) quantifies fill realism, slippage, gaps, intrabar ordering and P&L realism without changing that verdict. Engine facts verified against core/managed_strategy.py; order-type/intrabar/fill facts from the ntm3 NautilusTrader docs.

The expanded axes — execution realism & the six caveats

What the original three axes proved — and what they did not. The Time · Logic · Price loop proves the SL/Target level is computed correctly, trips on the right second, and that the realised fill equals the trigger bar's close. It does not prove the fill is realistic. This report adds a second, diagnostic tier covering the six caveats — it quantifies them per trade but never flips a Time·Logic·Price verdict, because every one of these is documented base-engine behaviour, not a bug.

New axisWhat it surfacesHow it's checked here
Entry correctnessThe MARKET entry fills at the signal bar's close (no next-bar-open look-ahead, no latency).Entry price reconciled against the bar feed; entries are MARKET/GTC on the EMA signal bar.
Realistic fillsThe reduce-only MARKET exit fills at the trigger bar's close, not at the SL/Target level.Per trade: Δ fill−lvl column. Fill==close already checked as the Price axis.
SlippageThe default FillModel applies zero slippage (prob_slippage=0.0).Reported as an engine fact + a conservative 1-tick-per-exit haircut on P&L.
Gap behaviourWhen a bar opens already past the level (intraday gap or an overnight hold), the close-fill can land far from the level. m-cube's manual market exit bypasses Nautilus' gap-aware native-stop fill.Per trade: a ↑gap marker + a count of gap-through and cross-session holds.
Intrabar orderingInside one bar the engine walks a fixed Open→High→Low→Close path (bar_adaptive_high_low_ordering off) and checks SL before TP.Dual-level files (VP-03/04, OT-05): count of same-bar SL+Target collisions where SL correctly won.
P&L realismThe headline caveat: a stop triggered on the bar's high/low but filled at the close gives an unrealistically good (or, on a gap, bad) exit, inflating/deflating performance.A fill-at-level counterfactual: every level exit re-priced AT its level (= a native move-through stop), reported as the net P&L inflation per case and overall.

Engine facts verified against core/managed_strategy.py and the ntm3 NautilusTrader 1.224.0 Backtesting concept doc (intrabar ordering, market-fill timing, FillModel/slippage defaults, gap handling).

Execution realism & P&L summary

Across 13 runnable level-exit cases, the close-fill model moved reported P&L by -864 vs a fill-at-level (native move-through stop): 96 exits filled favourably (flattering results by +980), 212 adverse (-1,844), of which 169 opened past the level and 13 were held into a later session. Largest single favourable fill: VP-03 +477.89 pts (+439 P&L). Largest single adverse fill: VP-03 -462.39 pts (-503 P&L). On top of this, slippage is zero — a 1-tick conservative slippage on every exit would remove a further −3.08.
⚑ Finding surfaced by the gap axis — overnight holds on a MIS portfolio. Every file is product="MIS" with a 15:29 IST square-off that (per the spec) should flatten any open position at the NSE close every session. Yet 13 feature exits were held into a later session and filled on their SL/Target at/after the next open — often through a large overnight gap [VP-03 (13)]. These cases log no Squareoff exits at all, whereas the no-feature cases (VP-11 / OT-06) do square off once per session. This is the largest single source of adverse fill realism here (e.g. VP-03 OrderID 2: SL level ~24728.7 → filled 24399.5, a −329pt overnight gap). Recommend the dev team confirm whether the daily MIS square-off is being bypassed when a leg has an SL/Target armed. (Reported as a diagnostic — it does not change the Time·Logic·Price verdicts, which only assert the level/trigger/fill are internally consistent.)

VP-01 Leg fixed SL % (long & short) PASS PASS:26

Setup: 1 leg · EMA(9/21) · SL = percentage 0.5% · no target.

A long sets its stop 0.5% below the entry; a short sets it 0.5% above. The stop should trip the instant price touches that level, and the position closes at that bar's price.
Technically: Long SL = round(F×0.995, 0.01); short SL = round(F×1.005, 0.01). Trigger = first 1-sec bar low≤SL (long) / high≥SL (short); realised fill = that bar's close (reduce-only MARKET close, so fill ≠ the level).
Entry correctness (D): 26/26 entries fill at the signal bar's close — MARKET/GTC, no next-bar-open look-ahead.
Execution realism (diagnostic — does not change the Time·Logic·Price verdict): of 12 level exits, 5 filled favourably (close beat the level → flatters P&L), 7 adverse, 0 ~at level · 6 gap-through (bar opened already past the level), 0 held into a later session.
P&L realism — reported close-fill vs a fill-at-level (what a native move-through stop would give): net -3 (favourable +8 / adverse -11) · best favourable +1.48 pts, worst adverse -3.54 pts. Slippage is zero by default; a conservative 1-tick slippage on every exit would remove a further −0.12.

VP-07 SL Wait (confirmation gate) PASS PASS:31

Setup: 1 leg · SL 0.4%, sl_wait_bars = 3.

When price first pierces the stop the exit is HELD; it only fires if the level holds for 3 bars. So the exit is deliberately later than the first touch.
Technically: Exit second = first-touch + (wait_bars − 1) bars. On the 1-second feed that is first_touch + 2s. We verify the delay is present and exactly that — first-touch == exit would be WRONG here.
All 17 stop exits confirmed the SL held for 3 bars before firing (the wait gate) — none fired on first touch.
Entry correctness (D): 31/31 entries fill at the signal bar's close — MARKET/GTC, no next-bar-open look-ahead.
